title: Damage found in bridge inspections
intro:
A state's bridge inspections record two kinds of damage. A = the deck shows cracking, found on **20 %** of bridges. B = a bearing shows corrosion, found on **15 %**. Both are found on **6 %** of bridges.

For a bridge chosen at random, find the probability that it has at least one of the two kinds of damage, the probability of deck cracking given that a bearing is corroded, and the probability of bearing corrosion given that the deck is cracked. Give each to three decimals or more.

ask.prompt: P(A ∪ B), at least one kind of damage
P(A | B), deck cracking given bearing corrosion
P(B | A), bearing corrosion given deck cracking

Union.says: You added P(A) and P(B). The 6 % of bridges with both kinds of damage are then counted twice: subtract P(A ∩ B) once.
You assumed the two kinds of damage are independent and used P(A)·P(B) for the overlap. The overlap is given: P(A ∩ B) = 0.06.

AGivenB.says: You divided by P(A). Given B means the bridges with corroded bearings are the new sample space: divide P(A ∩ B) by P(B).
That is P(A ∩ B), the share of all bridges with both. Given B, divide it by P(B).

BGivenA.says: You divided by P(B). Given A means the bridges with deck cracking are the new sample space: divide P(A ∩ B) by P(A).
That is P(A ∩ B), the share of all bridges with both. Given A, divide it by P(A).

hints: Write down what is given: P(A) = 0.20, P(B) = 0.15, P(A ∩ B) = 0.06.
At least one of the two is A ∪ B: P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B) and P(B | A) = P(A ∩ B) / P(A). A two-way table per 100 bridges may help: 6 have both, 14 only cracking, 9 only corrosion.
